findings.source_passage: all that stirs up the lees of things; all truth with malice in it; all that cracks the sinews and cakes the brain; all the subtle demonisms of life and thought; all evil
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'All that most maddens and torments'
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most critically cited rhetorical catalogs in the novel, defining what Moby Dick incarnates for Ahab; 'all that stirs up the lees of things' and 'all the subtle demonisms of life and thought' are both dropped, gutting the catalog's cumulative force and its specific interpretive content.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full catalog verbatim: 'All that most maddens and torments; all that stirs up the lees of things; all truth with malice in it; all that cracks the sinews and cakes the brain; all the subtle demonisms of life and thought; all evil, to crazy Ahab, were visibly personified, and made practically assailable in Moby Dick.'

findings.source_passage: that smiled on, as if at a birth or a bridal
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Judge, then, to what pitches of inflamed'
findings.why_it_matters: The doubled simile 'at a birth or a bridal' — both events of social celebration indifferent to suffering — is rhetorically pointed; dropping 'birth' reduces the ironic bite to a single, weaker image.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'as if at a birth or a bridal' verbatim.

findings.source_passage: I gave myself up to the abandonment of the time and the place
findings.why_it_matters: 'The time and the place' is the specific phrase Melville uses; 'the time and tide' shifts the meaning and introduces a nautical cliché foreign to the source.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'the time and the place' as written.

summary: The draft drops two phrases from the novel's most-quoted Ahab-monomania catalog ('all that stirs up the lees of things' and 'all the subtle demonisms of life and thought'), constituting a high-severity signature loss in a passage the critical tradition returns to constantly.
